newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds hard hit by U.S. markets.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds hard hit by U.S. markets.

text.p: Argentine bonds slumped sharply late Wednesday in the wake of a huge tumble by U.S. Treasuries.
Traders said there was genuine selling but one player commented that "I have not seen any big off-loading of positions."
Still, traders noted a negative signal at the surprising break by the FRB through key resistance at 85-1/4. The FRB was last down 1-3/8 at 84-7/8, the session's low.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 slumped $0.75 to 122.10.

Argentine bonds were hit by the double impact of a rise of more than 10 basis points in the 30-year U.S. bond yield to 6.23 percent and a drop of more than one percent in the Dow Jones Industrials .DJI.
"The market was very nervous," said another trader.

The market was further put out by the fact that there seemed to be no obvious fundamental reason for the sharp shift in mood in U.S. markets. "The big question now is whether the upward trend has finished or not," said the first trader.
For instance, U.S. producer price figures released Wednesday showed no alarming rise in inflation.
However, the selling spree hit the Argentine market with force, with Argentina's Par bond due 2023 by far the biggest casualty. It plummetted 2-1/8 to 61-1/4.

Traders were at a loss to predict the likely movement of Argentine bonds in coming days considering the heavy influence of U.S. markets on the Argentine one. "It's very difficult to say what will happen," said the first trader.
In the money markets, call money rates fell to 6.28 percent from 6.38 percent.
